description: ISP wireless device catalog with real-world specs, drawn from a mix of vendor datasheets, product pages, and FCC filings with varying verification depth. Per-field verification status is tracked in each device's `evidence` block (status legend: V, V(2nd), derived, UNVERIFIED, low-confidence).

devices.name: Ubiquiti airFiber 60
devices.notes: 60 GHz mmWave PTP. Requires clear LOS. Best for last-mile aggregation < 2 km.

max_throughput_mbps.note: Official FCC-filed manual says 1800 Mbps, NOT 1700 — catalog value not corrected.

max_range_km.note: Manual says '2+ km' — matches catalog's 2 as a rounded figure.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: 60 GHz radio gain matches (38 dBi), but this device also has a 5 GHz backup radio at 11 dBi gain that the catalog's single-radio model omits entirely.

tx_power_dbm.note: Manual says 25 dBm max conducted TX power (5/60 GHz combined), NOT 27 — catalog value not corrected.

frequency_ghz.note: Device is dual-radio: 60 GHz AND 5 GHz (U-NII) backup. Catalog's single `frequency_ghz:60` field cannot represent this — the 5 GHz backup radio is missing from the model entirely, not just imprecise.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: Not published in the official manual.

standard.note: Manual doesn't mention 802.11ad — OS is 'airOS GP', protocol proprietary.

devices.name: Ubiquiti airFiber 60 LR
devices.notes: Extended-range version of airFiber 60 with higher gain antenna.

max_throughput_mbps.note: Current official datasheet says 1950 Mbps, NOT 1700 — catalog value has not been corrected; this entry flags the mismatch, not a confirmation.

max_range_km.note: Current official datasheet says 12+ km, NOT 3.5 km — large discrepancy, catalog value not corrected.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: Older FCC-filed manual says 38 dBi, NOT 43 — current datasheet doesn't publish this figure at all.

tx_power_dbm.note: Not found in the current official datasheet or the older FCC manual — catalog's 27 dBm is not backed by any source found.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: Same as tx_power_dbm — not published by the vendor for this UISP-era model.

frequency_ghz.note: Vendor publishes a 57-71 GHz band, not a single figure — catalog's 60 is a loose simplification.

standard.note: Neither official document mentions 802.11ad — vendor calls the radio proprietary 'Wave Technology' under airOS.

devices.name: Ubiquiti LiteBeam 5AC Gen2
devices.notes: Low-cost CPE for WISP subscribers. airMAX AC protocol.

max_throughput_mbps.note: Vendor page says '450+ Mbps' — matches catalog.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: Datasheet and techspecs page agree: 23 dBi — matches catalog.

tx_power_dbm.note: Datasheet says 25 dBm output power, NOT 23 — catalog value not corrected.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: Datasheet gives a per-modulation table from -96 dBm (best, BPSK 1/2) to -65 dBm (worst, 256QAM 5/6) — no single published figure. Catalog's -95 is close to the best-case end but not a value the vendor states directly.

max_range_km.note: Vendor does not publish a maximum range figure anywhere (confirmed absent from both the datasheet PDF and the techspecs page).

frequency_ghz.note: Vendor publishes a 5150-5875 MHz band, not a single figure — catalog's 5.8 is a loose simplification.

standard.note: Datasheet calls it 'airMAX ac Protocol' (proprietary TDMA over 802.11ac PHY), not '802.11ac Wave 2' verbatim — plausible characterization, not the vendor's own term.

devices.name: Ubiquiti PowerBeam 5AC 400
devices.notes: Dual-feed dish for point-to-point links. Compact form factor.

tx_power_dbm.note: Datasheet (PBE-5AC-400 row): 25 dBm output power — matches catalog.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: Datasheet: 25 dBi — matches catalog.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: Per-modulation table row '2x QPSK (1/2)' is literally -95 dBm — matches catalog (not the best-case figure, but a value printed verbatim in the table).

max_throughput_mbps.note: Datasheet: 'up to 450+ Mbps real TCP/IP throughput' (family-wide claim) — matches catalog.

max_range_km.note: No range figure (km or miles) anywhere in the 11-page datasheet.

frequency_ghz.note: Vendor publishes 5150-5875 MHz worldwide band — catalog's 5.8 is a loose simplification.

standard.note: Datasheet calls it 'airMAX ac' (proprietary), not '802.11ac Wave 2' verbatim.

devices.name: Ubiquiti PowerBeam 5AC 620
devices.notes: Higher-gain dish variant. Ideal for long backhaul links.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: Official datasheet PBE-5AC-620 section states 29 dBi — matches catalog exactly.

max_throughput_mbps.note: Datasheet states 'up to 450+ Mbps real TCP/IP throughput' (family-wide claim) — matches catalog.

tx_power_dbm.note: Datasheet PBE-5AC-620 section states Output Power: 24 dBm, NOT 25 — catalog is 1 dB off, not corrected.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: RX table best case (1x BPSK 1/2) is -96 dBm literal, NOT -95 — catalog is 1 dB off, not corrected.

max_range_km.note: Vendor does not publish a range figure (km or miles) anywhere in the datasheet; catalog's 35 is not backed by any source found.

frequency_ghz.note: Datasheet states a 5 GHz band (PBE-5AC-620 section), not a single figure — catalog's 5.8 is a loose simplification.

standard.note: Datasheet calls it 'airMAX ac technology' (proprietary) — the terms '802.11ac'/'Wave 2' do not appear anywhere in the document.

devices.name: Ubiquiti airMAX M5
devices.notes: Base station radio. Paired with sector antenna. TDMA airMAX protocol.

tx_power_dbm.note: TX table for 802.11n: MCS0-3 = 27 dBm (best case) — matches catalog.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: RX table for 802.11n: MCS0 = -96 dBm (best case, literal table value) — matches catalog.

max_throughput_mbps.note: Family datasheet says 'supports speeds of up to 150+ Mbps real TCP/IP throughput' (RocketM family-wide claim) — matches catalog.

standard.note: Model-specific datasheet says '802.11n / Airmax Support Only at this Time' — matches catalog almost verbatim.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: This is a base-station radio sold without an integrated antenna (paired with an external sector/dish per catalog notes) — 0 is a reasonable convention for a radio-only SKU, same pattern as cambium-epmp1000/cambium-cnreach-n500.

frequency_ghz.note: Datasheet states Operating Frequency 5470-5825 MHz, not a single figure — catalog's 5.8 is a loose simplification.

max_range_km.note: Not published in either the model-specific or family datasheet; a third-party reseller page mentions '50km Range' but is not a primary source and was not used as evidence — catalog's 50 is not backed by any vendor source found.

devices.name: Ubiquiti Rocket 5AC Prism
devices.notes: High-capacity PTMP base station. Supports 4x4 MIMO sector antennas.

tx_power_dbm.note: Gen 1 datasheet (model R5AC-PRISM, matching catalog's model field exactly): 'R5AC-PRISM Output Power: 27 dBm' — matches catalog exactly. Note: the Gen 2 datasheet (different model RP-5AC-Gen2) states 28 dBm — do not confuse with Gen 1.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: Gen 1 RX table: 1x BPSK(1/2) = -96 dBm (best case) — matches catalog.

max_throughput_mbps.note: Gen 1 datasheet: 'airMAX ac Technology for up to 500+ Mbps Throughput' — matches catalog.

standard.note: Gen 1 datasheet calls it 'airMAX ac' (proprietary) — the terms '802.11ac'/'Wave 2' do not appear anywhere in the 494-line document.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: Base-station radio sold without an integrated antenna (paired with an external RocketDish/sector) — 0 is a reasonable convention.

frequency_ghz.note: Datasheet states worldwide 5150-5875 MHz band, not a single figure.

max_range_km.note: Not published in the Gen 1 datasheet (no km/mile section); catalog's 30 is not backed by any source found.

devices.name: MikroTik SXTsq 5
devices.notes: Budget PTMP CPE. RouterOS based. Good for dense subscriber deployments.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: Official product page: 16 dBi — matches catalog.

tx_power_dbm.note: Product page: 28 dBm max (at 6 Mbit/s / MCS0), NOT 23 — catalog value not corrected.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: Product page: -96 dBm best-case, catalog says -94 — 2 dB off from the best-case point, minor mismatch.

max_throughput_mbps.note: Vendor's own MEASURED bridging throughput (1518-byte, fast path) is 98.4 Mbps — same pattern as mikrotik-lhg5: catalog's 300 is roughly 3x the vendor's measured figure.

standard.note: Product page says '802.11a/n' — catalog drops the 802.11a mode.

frequency_ghz.note: Vendor publishes a 5 GHz band, not a single figure.

max_range_km.note: Not listed on the official product page. Product is also marked 'Discontinued' by the vendor (no lifecycle field exists in this catalog schema).

devices.name: MikroTik LHG 5
devices.notes: Lightweight grid antenna CPE. Excellent range-to-cost ratio.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: Official product page: 24.5 dBi — matches catalog.

tx_power_dbm.note: Product page: 25 dBm max (at 6 Mbit/s / MCS0), NOT 23 — catalog value not corrected.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: Product page: -96 dBm best-case (6 Mbit/s / MCS0), catalog says -95 — 1 dB off, minor mismatch.

max_throughput_mbps.note: Vendor's own MEASURED bridging throughput (1518-byte packets) is 98.4 Mbps — catalog claims 300, roughly 3x higher than the vendor's measured figure.

standard.note: Product page says '802.11a/n' — catalog drops the 802.11a mode, minor but not strictly correct.

frequency_ghz.note: Vendor publishes a band (5150-5875 MHz intl / 5170-5250 & 5725-5835 MHz US) — catalog's 5.8 is a loose simplification.

max_range_km.note: Not listed on the official product page.

devices.name: MikroTik LHG 5 AC
devices.notes: AC upgrade of LHG. 2x2 MIMO chain. Suitable for high-throughput backhaul.

model.note: Official MikroTik product page lists the model as 'RBLHGG-5acD' (two G's) — catalog's 'RBLHG-5acD' (one G) is close but not the exact official model string; appears to be a single dropped letter rather than a fabricated model.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: Official spec table: 24.5 dBi — matches catalog exactly.

tx_power_dbm.note: TX-per-datarate table: 6Mbit/s=25dBm, MCS0=25dBm (best), 54Mbit/s=21dBm, MCS7=20dBm, MCS9=18dBm — no row equals 22 dBm, catalog does not match any published row.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: RX table: 6Mbit/s=-96, MCS0=-96 (best case) — catalog's -95 is 1 dB off from the best-case point.

max_throughput_mbps.note: Official max PHY data rate is 867 Mbit/s; measured Ethernet bridging (fast path, 1518-byte) is 998.2 Mbps — catalog's 500 UNDERSTATES both published figures (opposite direction from the older -nD generation MikroTik SKUs, which overstate).

standard.note: Official page says '802.11a/n/ac' — catalog drops the a/n modes, minor but not strictly accurate.

frequency_ghz.note: Official page states 5150-5875 MHz (International) band, not a single figure.

max_range_km.note: Official product page does not list a range figure; catalog's 20 is not backed by any source found.

devices.name: MikroTik Dynadish 5
devices.notes: High-gain dish for long-distance PTP. Dual-chain AC radio.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: RX table: 6Mbit/s=-96, MCS0=-96 (best case, literal table value) — matches catalog.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: Official page repeatedly states '25dBi antenna gain' (description and spec table) — catalog's 28 is 3 dBi higher than official, does not match.

tx_power_dbm.note: TX-per-datarate table: 6Mbit/s=31dBm, MCS0=30dBm, 54Mbit/s=28dBm, MCS7=27dBm, MCS9=22dBm — no row equals 24 dBm; also, the RX row that matched above (-96 dBm) pairs with TX 30-31dBm in the same table, not 24 — catalog's tx/rx pair appears mixed from different data-rate rows.

max_throughput_mbps.note: Official max PHY data rate is 867 Mbit/s; measured Ethernet bridging (fast path) is 986.1 Mbps — catalog's 700 UNDERSTATES both, same pattern as mikrotik-lhg5-ac.

standard.note: Official page says '802.11a/n/ac' — catalog drops the a/n modes, minor.

frequency_ghz.note: Official page states 5150-5875 MHz band, not a single figure.

max_range_km.note: Official product page does not list a range figure; catalog's 30 is not backed by any source found.

devices.name: MikroTik RB911G-5HPnD
devices.notes: High-power basestation board. Requires external sector antenna.

tx_power_dbm.note: TX table: 6Mbit/s=30dBm, MCS0=30dBm (best case, two rows match literally) — matches catalog exactly.

max_throughput_mbps.note: Official page states 'Wireless 5 GHz Max data rate: 300 Mbit/s' (explicit official field, not measured Ethernet bridging) — matches catalog exactly.

standard.note: Official page says '802.11a/n' — catalog drops the 'a' mode, minor but consistent with other MikroTik SKUs.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: This is a bare routerboard radio without an integrated antenna (paired via external MMCX connector to a sector) — 0 is a reasonable convention, same pattern as ePMP 1000/Rocket M5.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: RX table: 6Mbit/s=-96, MCS0=-96 (best case), 54Mbit/s=-78, MCS7=-75 — no row equals -94 dBm; catalog is 2 dB off from the best-case point.

frequency_ghz.note: Official page states 5150-5875 MHz band, not a single figure.

max_range_km.note: Official product page does not list a range figure; catalog's 20 is not backed by any source found.

devices.name: TP-Link CPE510
devices.notes: Entry-level outdoor CPE. 13 dBi dual-polarized antenna. Pharos protocol.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: Datasheet: 'Gain: 13dBi' — matches catalog exactly.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: RF specifications table, 802.11n row: MCS0 = -93 dBm (and MCS8 = -93 dBm) — matches catalog exactly, literal table value.

max_range_km.note: Datasheet: 'System-level optimizations for more than 15km+ long range wireless transmission' — matches catalog (phrased as a lower bound, not a precise single figure, but consistent).

max_throughput_mbps.note: Datasheet: 'Wireless Speed: Up to 300Mbps (40MHz, Dynamic)' — matches catalog exactly.

standard.note: Datasheet: 'Wireless Standards: IEEE 802.11a/n (with Pharos MAXtream disabled)' — catalog drops the 802.11a mode, minor, same pattern as MikroTik SKUs.

tx_power_dbm.note: Datasheet: 'Maximum Transmit Power: 27dBm/500mW (Adjustable power by 1dBm)'; RF table also shows nearly all rows at 27dBm (MCS6=26, MCS7=25) — catalog's 23 is 4 dB below the published maximum, not corrected.

frequency_ghz.note: Datasheet states 'Operating Frequency: 5.15~5.85GHz' band, not a single figure.

devices.name: TP-Link CPE610
devices.notes: Higher-gain 23 dBi panel variant. Good for suburban WISP deployments.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: Consistent across the 2018 flyer, 2025 datasheet, and product page: 23 dBi — matches catalog exactly.

max_throughput_mbps.note: Consistent across both datasheets: 'Up to 300 Mbps (40 MHz, Dynamic)' — matches catalog exactly.

tx_power_dbm.note: Two official documents disagree with each other: 2018 flyer states 27 dBm, 2025 datasheet + product page state 25 dBm — catalog's 23 does NOT match either version.

standard.note: Both documents say 'IEEE 802.11a/n' — catalog drops the 802.11a mode, minor, consistent pattern.

frequency_ghz.note: Datasheets state a 5.15-5.85 GHz band, not a single figure.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: Not found in either the 2018 flyer or the 2025 family datasheet (unlike tplink-cpe510, which has an individual datasheet with a per-MCS RX table); the individual 'CPE610-Datasheet.pdf' on static.tp-link.com returns 404. Catalog's -93 is not backed by any source found.

max_range_km.note: Not published in either datasheet family (no range section at all, unlike CPE510 which explicitly states '15km+'). Catalog's 20 is not backed by any source found.

devices.name: TP-Link CPE710
devices.notes: AC upgrade of CPE610. Dual-band capable. Best value AC CPE from TP-Link.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: Datasheet: 23 dBi — matches catalog exactly.

max_throughput_mbps.note: Datasheet: 'Up to 867 Mbps (80 MHz, Dynamic)' — matches catalog exactly.

tx_power_dbm.note: Datasheet and product page agree: 27 dBm Maximum Transmit Power (no source conflict, unlike CPE610) — catalog's 23 is 4 dB below the published maximum, not corrected.

standard.note: Datasheet says 'IEEE 802.11a/n/ac' — catalog drops the a/n modes, minor, consistent pattern.

frequency_ghz.note: Datasheet states a 5.15-5.85 GHz band, not a single figure.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: Not found in the datasheet family or product page (no RX sensitivity table at all), same dead end as CPE610; individual 'CPE710-Datasheet.pdf' on static.tp-link.com returns 404. Catalog's -95 is not backed by any source found.

max_range_km.note: Not published — product page only states qualitatively 'long-distance application'/'long-range point-to-point', no km/mile figure anywhere. Catalog's 25 is not backed by any source found.

devices.name: Cambium ePMP 1000
devices.notes: GPS-synchronized TDD PTMP base station. Reduces co-channel interference in dense deployments.

model.note: Catalog's model 'C050900C001A' does NOT appear among the 5 official sales model numbers for the ePMP 1000 GPS Sync Radio family (C050900A011A / C050900A112A / C050900A013A / C050900A211A / C050900P011A), nor in a separate web search for the exact string. Could be a typo, an older/unindexed revision, or fabricated — not resolved.

tx_power_dbm.note: Spec sheet gives a range (-17 to +30 dBm combined, to regional EIRP limit). Catalog's 27 falls inside that range but is not a published single figure.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: Spec sheet gives -93 dBm (MCS0, 20 MHz) down to -69 dBm (MCS15) — catalog's -94 is close to but not an exact match for any published row.

max_throughput_mbps.note: Spec sheet: 'more than 200 Mbps of real user throughput' — consistent with catalog's 200 (vendor says '>200', catalog states it as an exact figure).

standard.note: Spec sheet explicitly says 'Cambium Proprietary' MAC layer, NOT 802.11n — catalog's standard label does not match.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: This radio is sold without an integrated antenna (paired with an external sector) — 0 is a reasonable convention for a 'radio-only' SKU, not verified against a specific published figure.

frequency_ghz.note: Vendor publishes a 4910-5970 MHz band, not a single figure.

max_range_km.note: Not listed in the spec sheet.

devices.name: Cambium ePMP 3000
devices.notes: MU-MIMO 4x4 sector AP. Serves up to 120 SMs per sector.

model.note: Catalog's model 'C058900D001A' does not appear in the official Ordering Information (radio models follow the pattern C0509xxAxxxA/C0589xxAxxxA, e.g. C058910A102A; antenna is C050910D301A). A separate web search for the exact string found no relevant match. Could be a typo of the real model or fabricated — not resolved. This is the second ePMP SKU in this audit with an unmatched model number (after cambium-epmp1000), suggesting a systematic issue rather than an isolated typo.

standard.note: Datasheet: 'The ePMP 3000 Access Point series is the third generation based on 802.11ac Wave 2 technology' — matches catalog almost verbatim.

tx_power_dbm.note: Datasheet gives a range: 'Transmit Power: 0 to +32 dBm (combined, to regional EIRP limit) (1 dB interval)'. Catalog's 27 falls inside that range but is not a published single figure.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: Sold as a radio separate from the optional sector antenna (Part # C050910D301A) — 0 is a reasonable convention for a radio-only SKU.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: Nominal Receive Sensitivity @20 MHz channel for the ePMP 3000 model (not 3000L/MicroPOP): MCS0 = -92 dBm (best case) — catalog's -96 claims 4 dB MORE sensitivity than the official maximum, does not match.

max_range_km.note: Not listed in the datasheet (no km/mile section). Catalog's 30 is not backed by any source found.

max_throughput_mbps.note: Two different official figures found: 1.2 Gbps aggregate per sector ('120+ subscribers') vs 600 Mbps aggregate per Force 300 SM — catalog's 800 does not match either published figure, appears to sit between them without a clear basis.

frequency_ghz.note: Datasheet states 'Wide Band Operation 4910-5970 MHz', not a single figure.

devices.name: Cambium PMP 450i
devices.notes: Carrier-grade PTMP platform. Higher reliability and range than 802.11 PTMP. Licensed-band variants available.

standard.note: Datasheet: MAC 'Cambium Networks proprietary'; PHY '2x2 MIMO OFDM' — matches catalog.

max_throughput_mbps.note: Datasheet: '2x2 OFDM MIMO radio capable of up to 300 Mbps per sector in a 40 MHz channel' — matches catalog exactly.

max_range_km.note: Datasheet: 'Maximum Deployment Range: Up to 40 miles (64 km)' — catalog's 40 appears to have been taken from the MILES column and mislabeled as km (40 miles = 64 km); same unit-confusion pattern confirmed in cambium-pmp450m — a suspected bug, not corrected here.

tx_power_dbm.note: Datasheet: 'Maximum Transmit Power: +28 dBm (MIMO, combined H+V)' for the 5 GHz variant (+25 dBm for the 3 GHz variant) — catalog's 30 is 2 dB above the published maximum for the 5 GHz variant, does not match.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: Datasheet is ambiguous across variants: Connectorized (gain 0, external antenna) vs Integrated 90/120-degree Sector (17 dBi +/-1) vs Integrated 10-degree Sector (23 dBi +/-1) — catalog does not specify which variant this SKU represents. If connectorized, 0 is reasonable; if an integrated-sector AP (the more common 'AP' representation), it is off by 17-23 dB, same architecture inconsistency as cambium-pmp450m.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: Datasheet only gives a required-SNR table per modulation (QPSK 10dB, 16QAM 17dB, 64QAM 24dB, 256QAM 32dB) — no absolute dBm sensitivity table exists. Cannot be derived from SNR alone without assuming a noise floor. Catalog's -93 is not backed by any source found.

frequency_ghz.note: Datasheet states a 5 GHz band (4900-5925 MHz; also a separate 3 GHz variant at 3300-3900 MHz), not a single figure.

devices.name: Cambium PMP 450m
devices.notes: Massive MIMO 16x2 AP. Highest capacity Cambium PMP platform. Up to 2 Gbps aggregate.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: Datasheet: 'Ultimate Sensitivity: -94 dBm' — matches catalog exactly.

max_throughput_mbps.note: Vendor's own highest published claim is 'more than 1.2 Gbps in a 40 MHz channel' — catalog's 2000 Mbps EXCEEDS the vendor's own stated maximum (1200).

max_range_km.note: Datasheet: 'Maximum Deployment Range: Up to 64 km (40 miles)'. Catalog's 40 looks like it was taken from the miles column and mislabeled as km — a suspected unit-confusion bug, not corrected here.

standard.note: Datasheet: MAC 'Cambium Networks proprietary', PHY '14x14 Multi-User MIMO OFDM' — catalog's 'Proprietary MU-MIMO' label is the most accurate of any SKU in this audit.

tx_power_dbm.note: Datasheet states Maximum EIRP +45 dBm for the integrated 90-degree sector antenna — catalog's tx_power_dbm:30 + antenna_gain_dbi:0 (implying ~30 dBm EIRP) is architecturally inconsistent with this being a sectorized AP, not a bare radio; ~15 dB short of the published EIRP.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: Same inconsistency as tx_power_dbm above — this SKU has an integrated sector antenna, so gain 0 doesn't fit the product architecture.

frequency_ghz.note: Vendor publishes a 5150-5925 MHz band. Also note: this datasheet verifies the 5 GHz variant (14x14 MIMO); Cambium also sells a 3 GHz PMP 450m variant (8x8 MIMO, per registry.md B07) with different specs — catalog's generic id doesn't state which band, so this evidence may not apply if the SKU is meant to represent the 3 GHz variant.

devices.name: Cambium cnPilot e500
devices.notes: Outdoor dual-band Wi-Fi AP for hotspot and enterprise campus deployments. IP67.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: Datasheet: 'ANTENNA GAIN: 5 dBi' (integrated 360-degree omni antenna, dual-polarized 2x2 MIMO) — catalog's 6 is 1 dB off, does not match exactly.

tx_power_dbm.note: Datasheet: 'TRANSMIT POWER: 29 dBm @ 2.4GHz, 28 dBm @ 5GHz' (separate dual-band radios) — catalog's 26 is below both published radio values.

max_range_km.note: Datasheet: 'MAX RANGE — Client: 213 m (700 Ft)' (mesh figures differ: 2.4GHz 3000m, 5GHz 1500m, different context) — catalog's 0.3 km rounds up from 213 m (0.213 km), close but not an exact match.

max_throughput_mbps.note: Datasheet states 'MAX DATA RATES: 1.01 Gbps' (aggregate dual-radio) — catalog's 867 Mbps looks like a generic 802.11ac 5GHz VHT80 3-stream PHY-rate figure commonly used in marketing, but does not appear as a literal number in this Cambium datasheet, which instead states an aggregate throughput of 1.01 Gbps.

frequency_ghz.note: Datasheet describes a dual-band radio: 2.4 GHz (2.4-2.4835 GHz) AND 5 GHz (5.15-5.85 GHz) — catalog's single frequency_ghz:5.8 omits the entire 2.4 GHz radio, same architecture-simplification pattern as ubnt-airfiber60.

standard.note: Main datasheet calls it an '802.11ac Gigabit outdoor Access Point' without the literal words 'Wave 2'; a secondary source (search snippet) mentions 'dual radio 802.11ac wave 2 technology' but was not the primary document read — plausible characterization, not verbatim from the primary source.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: Not listed in this datasheet (no per-MCS sensitivity table). Catalog's -95 is not backed by any source found.

devices.name: Cambium cnReach N500

tx_power_dbm.note: Spec sheet: ISM mode 10 dBm-30 dBm (10mW-1W) max — matches catalog's 30 exactly as the ISM-mode maximum.

standard.note: Modulations explicitly listed: MSK/2FSK/BPSK/QPSK/8PSK/16PSK/16QAM/32QAM (ISM) and MSK/4FSK/QPSK/8PSK/16QAM/32QAM/64QAM (MAS) — the word 'OFDM' does not appear anywhere in the document. 'Proprietary' is accurate, 'OFDM' is not backed by this source.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: Radio is sold with external RF TNC connector(s) (1 or 2 depending on single/dual-radio), no integrated antenna mentioned — 0 is a reasonable convention, same pattern as cambium-epmp1000.

frequency_ghz.note: Two separate bands: ISM 902-928 MHz; MAS 928-960 MHz — catalog's single 0.9 is a loose simplification.

devices.name: Ubiquiti AM-5AC21-60
devices.notes: 60-degree sector antenna. Pairs with Rocket AC base station radios.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: Datasheet (AM-5AC21-60 model section and characteristics table): 21 dBi — matches catalog exactly.

frequency_ghz.note: Datasheet states 'Frequency Range: 5.10 - 5.85 GHz', not a single figure.

tx_power_dbm.note: This is a passive antenna with no integrated radio (paired with a separate Rocket radio — datasheet explicitly states 'Rocket radio sold separately') — all-zero radio fields correctly reflect the product architecture, the most consistent SKU in the whole audit.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: Same as tx_power_dbm — passive antenna, no radio to have a sensitivity figure.

max_range_km.note: Same as tx_power_dbm — passive antenna has no range of its own, depends on the paired radio.

max_throughput_mbps.note: Same as tx_power_dbm — passive antenna has no throughput of its own.

standard.note: Datasheet categorizes it as a 'BaseStation Sector Antenna' with no PHY/MAC (no radio) — consistent with catalog's 'passive' label conceptually.

devices.name: MikroTik OmniTIK 5 PoE
devices.notes: Omnidirectional 360-degree PTMP AP. RouterOS built-in 5-port switch.

tx_power_dbm.note: TX table: 54Mbit/s=27dBm (exact match for this row; other rows: 6Mbit/s=30, MCS0=30, MCS7=26) — matches catalog.

max_throughput_mbps.note: Official page states 'Wireless 5 GHz Max data rate: 300 Mbit/s' (explicit official field) — matches catalog exactly.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: Official page: 'Antenna gain dBi for 5 GHz: 7.5' (also stated in the product title '7.5dBi Integrated AP') — catalog's 9 is 1.5 dBi higher, does not match.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: RX table: 6Mbit/s=-96, MCS0=-96, 54Mbit/s=-78, MCS7=-75 — no row equals -93 dBm; also, the TX row that matched above (27dBm at 54Mbit/s) pairs with RX=-78 in the same table, not -93 — catalog's tx/rx pair appears mixed from different data-rate rows, same pattern as mikrotik-dynadish5.

standard.note: Official page says '802.11a/n' — catalog drops the 'a' mode, minor, consistent pattern.

frequency_ghz.note: Official page states 5150-5875 MHz band, not a single figure.

max_range_km.note: Official product page does not list a range figure; catalog's 5 is not backed by any source found.
